page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-4-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4n family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 7.75 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include GPU resources, and local storage is configured as None. It also does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With dedicated CPU allocation, the instance provides consistent compute performance without resource sharing. The high memory density relative to the vCPU count positions this server for memory-bound workloads rather than compute-heavy parallel processing. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration represents a tradeoff, requiring external block storage for persistent data and limiting its utility for hardware-accelerated tasks. Qualitatively, the hardware profile offers a resource-dense memory configuration for applications requiring moderate compute but larger memory footprints, optimizing costs by avoiding the need to scale up to higher vCPU tiers merely to obtain sufficient RAM.

This server configuration is suitable for workloads such as small-to-medium databases, in-memory caching systems, enterprise application backends, and memory-intensive web serving. It is also applicable for lightweight data processing pipelines that require substantial memory buffers but do not demand high multi-core CPU scaling or local disk throughput.
